system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: The large transfer itself is consistent with the approved backup workflow: stsync.exe ran as svc-archive with the StratoSafe ingest target, and proxy telemetry records 640,000,000 client-to-server bytes to that approved host.

Shortly before that backup process started, the domain controller recorded a Kerberos service-ticket request for svc-archive from public IP 139.162.174.124, followed by a service logon for svc-archive on FILE-NWD-01. The inventory says there is no VPN, so this source is unexplained and suspicious.
An unlisted Meridian service-healthcheck.exe ran as SYSTEM and connected through the proxy to receiver.citrix.com, which is not among the approved services provided in the environment context.

At 14:14, PROXY-NWD-01 attempted an RDP connection to FILE-NWD-01 and failed to log on as svc_mgmt; FILE-NWD-01 then made an SSH connection to the proxy and an SMB attempt to the domain controller, where svc_mgmt authentication also failed because the account was disabled. This pattern is unexplained by the stated proxy and remote-administration roles.

The file server also had an RDP session from the designated IT workstation, authenticated as sam.okafor; this is consistent with the approved administration source, though the supplied records do not show the stated patching command being run.

known_telemetry_limitations: Proxy and connection records show destination and byte counts, but not the contents of the transferred data.
The supplied records do not provide file-access or backup-job contents to establish what data stsync.exe uploaded.
The records show the anomalous authentication and connection events but do not establish who initiated them or whether the external source address reflects a logging or network-translation issue.
claims_not_established: The 640,000,000-byte transfer is not established to contain stolen data; its recorded process, account, and destination match the approved backup workflow.
The evidence does not establish why svc-archive was requested from the public IP, or whether that source reflects compromised credentials, an unexpected network intermediary, or a telemetry error.

The evidence does not establish that Meridian ServiceHealth is malicious, only that its recorded execution and Citrix connection are unexplained by the supplied approved-software and service inventory.
The evidence does not establish that the failed svc_mgmt attempts succeeded or that data was accessed through them.
additional_evidence_needed: Validate the 139.162.174.124 Kerberos source against DC, firewall, NAT, and identity-provider records; determine whether svc-archive credentials or tickets were exposed or misused.
Verify the StratoSafe job configuration, execution schedule, signed binary, uploaded file manifest, and destination-side backup records.
Identify the origin, installation history, signer, hash, and owner of Meridian ServiceHealth; review its service configuration and network activity.
Collect detailed authentication and endpoint records around 14:14, including account status history for svc_mgmt and any related process or service activity on PROXY-NWD-01 and FILE-NWD-01.
Review FILE-NWD-01 file-access, service, and scheduled-task logs for the period, and confirm whether the authorized workstation session performed the documented patching workflow.
